content:
Qualcomm and Apple have extended their global patent licensing agreement, which was originally set to expire in 2027. Here are the details.

The renewal takes effect next year

It is no exaggeration to say that the relationship between Apple and Qualcomm has been full of ups and downs.

The two companies were once major business partners, but in 2017 they became embroiled in a protracted legal battle over Qualcomm's patent licensing practices and royalty issues.

In short, Apple sued Qualcomm in U.S. federal court in early 2017, challenging its patent licensing practices and seeking to recover nearly $1 billion in patent fee rebates that Qualcomm allegedly wrongfully withheld.

Just three days before this lawsuit was filed, the U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) had also sued Qualcomm, alleging anticompetitive licensing practices. The complaint specifically referenced Qualcomm's dealings with Apple, claiming that Qualcomm offered billions of dollars in conditional rebates in exchange for Apple's exclusive use of Qualcomm modem chips in new iPhones and iPads.

Several months later, Qualcomm countersued Apple, alleging breach of contract and interference with its relationships with iPhone and iPad manufacturers.

The dispute came to an end in 2019, when Apple and Qualcomm agreed to withdraw all lawsuits between them worldwide.

As part of the settlement, Apple paid Qualcomm an undisclosed sum to resolve the royalty dispute over fees withheld during the litigation. The two companies also signed a six-year global patent licensing agreement along with a multi-year chipset supply agreement.

That licensing agreement took effect on April 1, 2019, and included an option for Apple to extend it by two years. Apple ultimately exercised that option, extending the agreement to March 2027.

Qualcomm announced today (the 24th) that the two parties have renewed the agreement once again, with the new contract taking effect on April 1, 2027.

Here is the full press release:

Qualcomm Incorporated announced today the renewal of its global patent licensing agreement with Apple, with the new agreement taking effect on April 1, 2027. John Han, Executive Vice President and General Manager of Qualcomm Technology Licensing (QTL), said: "We are pleased to extend our licensing agreement with Apple."

Qualcomm did not disclose the duration of the renewed agreement, and Apple has yet to respond to the renewal.

It is worth noting that this announcement has nothing to do with Apple's use of Qualcomm modems in iPhones — a topic that has attracted much attention recently, as the U.S. version of the iPhone 18 Pro Max uses a Qualcomm modem, while other regions use Apple's in-house C2 modem.

Apple has not yet officially commented on its future modem plans, but the market generally expects the company to eventually phase out Qualcomm modems entirely.
